title: Galaxies in the Fornax Cluster

recognition.text: Official NSF NOIRLab / Gemini press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Galaxies belonging to the Fornax Cluster are spread across this view from the Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope, which is located at Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory (CTIO). A few of the points of light are much closer foreground stars in our own Milky Way.

The cluster appears in the constellation Fornax, the Furnace, and is relatively nearby for a galaxy cluster, at only about 60 million light-years. A galaxy cluster is a large collection of galaxies held together by gravity, and its members can include smooth ellipticals as well as spirals, all moving through the cluster and sometimes interacting.

Because the Fornax Cluster is comparatively close, it gives astronomers a chance to study the galaxies of a cluster in more detail than distant ones allow. CTIO, where the telescope stands, is a Program of NSF NOIRLab, and the image was made with its Dark Energy Camera through three filters.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (43.80 x 21.90 arcminutes) and distance (60 million light years), the frame spans roughly 764,000 × 382,000 light-years. Its light set out about 60 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Taken with DECam on the Blanco 4-meter Telescope through g, r and i filters. The colour mapping isn't published.
